Use Nx = 400 finite-volume cells on the domain [-1, 1], giving dx = 0.005.
Use cell centers x_j = -1 + (j + 0.5)*dx for j = 0, ..., 399, with periodic wrap (no duplicated endpoint).
Evolve the conservative variables U = [rho, m, E] as cell averages for the 1D compressible Navier-Stokes system with m = rho*v, E = p/(Gamma-1) + 0.5*rho*v^2, Gamma = 1.6666666666666667, eta = 0.1, zeta = eta = 0.1, and viscous stress sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x.
Compute the pressure from the equation of state p = (Gamma-1)*(E - 0.5*m^2/rho), clipping rho and p to a floor of 1e-12 if needed.
Use the Rusanov (local Lax-Friedrichs) flux for the inviscid part with interface speed a = max(|v_L| + c_L, |v_R| + c_R) and c = sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Compute v_x with centered differences on cell-centered v values, form sigma, average sigma and v to interfaces, and add the viscous flux F_visc = [0, -sigma, -v*sigma] to the convective flux.
Enforce periodic boundary conditions by wrapping indices.
Integrate in time with the 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun) method on the semi-discrete finite-volume system.
Choose dt each step as min(dt_conv, dt_visc) with dt_conv = CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j| + c_j) and dt_visc = 0.5*dx^2/max(zeta + 4/3*eta, 1e-30), using CFL = 0.4, and adjust the last step to hit T = 0.5 exactly.
Set the initial conditions rho(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0) = 0.1*cos(pi*x), p(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*cos(pi*x) evaluated at the cell centers, with trig arguments in radians.
At T = 0.5, compute rho, v, p on the cell centers.
Save the arrays x, rho, v, p (each 1D of length 400) and the scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL to the file solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz.
Save a 3-panel line plot of rho, v, p versus x at T to solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png.
Print the min and max of rho and p (positivity check) and the mean of rho over the domain (mass conservation check).
Interpret '^' as exponentiation in the math and use '**' in Python code.
